The game tasks one to two players taking alternate turns with filling the shoes of short order Sam, as he attempts to fill the custom orders of the patrons of the grill, a hopping burger joint that that has installed an automated open flame oven, complete with conveyor belt and a food dispenser. Too bad, there's a glitch in the system as the oven keeps churning out plain burgers and the dispenser seems to randomly toss out the tomatoes, onions, lettuce, and cheese that short order Sam has to catch and slap on the hamburgers. Assuming, of course, those are the ingredients the customers have requested. If Sam is presented with a condiment that he doesn't need, the player must press the fire button on the Atari joystick stick to have Sam bounce it back into the dispenser with his rotund belly. Using the electronic order board at the bottom of the screen, Sam can keep track of which ingredients he will need for each burger. These are random, and as you can see in this video, I've got quite a few guests lining up for onions on their burger. After filling an order correctly, the food dispenser will shoot out the top bun. Sam then will take the completed burger to the wrapping room, depositing it hopefully in the correct color-coded wrapping chute, and not dropping it on the floor of the room. which is shockingly easy to do in the later levels when the conveyor belt is stacked up with burgers and you are constantly on the run. In Pressure Cooker you don't have a set number of lives but a performance rating which starts at 50 points. You can see the performance point value to the left of the open flame oven. You can gain or lose performance points depending on how well you're playing the game. The performance points are different than your score by the way. You will get 10 performance points every time you earn 10,000 points. points. The maximum number of performance points you can have is 99. Short order Sam will lose 1 performance point if he allows an ingredient to be wasted, whether that be smashing against Sam or against the conveyor belt. You will also lose 1 point if you happen to place the same type of ingredient on a hamburger more than once. Sam will lose 5 performance points every time he drops a hamburger into the wrong wrapping chute, or you miss the chute and you end up dropping it on the floor. Sam loses a whopping 10 performance points if a hamburger falls off the conveyor belt. Now about the scoring for Pressure Cooker. The player will get five points for every ingredient caught, 10 points for placing the condiment on a burger for the first time, 100 points for dropping the completed burger in the correct color-coded wrapping chute. The remaining performance points will be added to your score as efficiency bonus points at the end of the wave, as well as the completed burgers as they are sold, all raising your score before a new wave begins. With the difficulty increasing, I've advanced the difficulty of this wave to show you just how fast and frantic things can get in Pressure Cooker.
